title: Repo-wide runtime-loadability gate so the missing-bridge defect cannot recur
description:
Objective: add ONE gate that proves every workspace package loads under plain Node, so the missing-.js-bridge defect can never again reach a green board. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09. This is the durable fix; the per-package sweeps (task-eb9ff081, task-386fcb4c, task-b7049554, task-17b03331) are the cleanup.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST VALUABLE OF THE FOUR. The same defect has now been found FIVE separate times, each by a different agent, each time by accident, and each time only after it blocked something: @moe/runner (QA flagged it while approving supervisor child 1, then it blocked task-ba3a45f9), and now @moe/core, @moe/context, @moe/review, @moe/skills, @moe/mcp and @moe/control-room-client - six packages failing in a single probe. It keeps recurring because NOTHING IN THE REPO CHECKS IT. vitest rewrites a `./foo.js` specifier back to `foo.ts`, so every one of the ~2870 passing tests is structurally blind to it (mem:gotcha-vitest-hides-missing-js-bridge). A per-package sweep fixes today's instances; only a gate stops tomorrow's.

MEASURED 2026-08-09, the evidence this task generalizes. Probing each package's source entry with `node --experimental-strip-types`:
  PASS: scheduler(36 exports) store(26) runner(66) contracts(46) coordination(14) testkit(11) apps/daemon(1)
  FAIL: core, context, review, skills, mcp, control-room-client - each ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming a specific unbridged sibling
Bridge coverage is correspondingly inconsistent: store 53ts/49js, runner 52/45, scheduler 42/40, contracts 15/14, coordination 11/10 versus core 34/4, testkit 41/15, and context/review/skills/mcp/control-room-client at zero.

METHODOLOGY WARNING, learned the hard way while gathering the numbers above. My first probe ran `import('@moe/<name>')` by bare package name from the repo root and reported ALL TEN packages failing - including @moe/scheduler, which is correctly bridged. That was a probe artifact (bare workspace names do not resolve from the root), not a finding, and only a passing control revealed it. THE GATE MUST CARRY ITS OWN CONTROLS or it will one day report a repo-wide catastrophe that is really a harness bug, and be disabled for crying wolf.

Deliverable: a single test that enumerates workspace packages from pnpm-workspace.yaml (never a hand-maintained list, which would silently miss a new package - exactly the failure mode this gate exists to prevent), resolves each one's declared entry from its package.json "exports", spawns plain Node with --experimental-strip-types to import it, and asserts it resolves AND that its exports are defined rather than merely present. Failures name the package and the unresolvable specifier.

SCOPE DECISION FOR THE ARCHITECT: six packages fail today. A gate that fails immediately is useless as a merge gate but valuable as a truth source. Choose ONE and state it in the plan: either land the gate red and let the four sweep tasks turn it green, or land it with an explicit, individually-justified, dated allowlist of the six known-failing packages that shrinks to zero as they land. Do NOT weaken the assertion itself, and do NOT let an allowlist entry outlive its sweep task - an unreviewed permanent allowlist is how a gate becomes decoration.

NOT in scope: adding bridges to any package (that is the four sweep tasks); changing any package's exports map; a build step.

Hard dependencies: none. It measures whatever exists.

Owned paths: tests/runtime/** (new) and a root package.json script entry if a new lane is needed (ownership amendment - request it, do not assume it).
Verification: the new gate runs and reports honestly, plus pnpm typecheck and pnpm test still exit 0.
definitionOfDone: A single test enumerates workspace packages by reading pnpm-workspace.yaml and the package.json "exports" of each, never from a hand-maintained list — proven by a test asserting the discovered package set equals the directories on disk, so a newly added package is covered automatically on the day it appears.

For each package it spawns plain Node with --experimental-strip-types, imports the declared entry, and asserts BOTH that the import resolved AND that the namespace's exports are defined — not merely that the process exited 0, and not merely that a binding is present, since a TDZ-undefined binding from an import cycle imports fine and fails at first use.

THE GATE CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROLS: a known-good bridged package must PASS and a deliberately unresolvable specifier must FAIL with the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, both asserted inside the suite. Without them a harness bug reports a repo-wide catastrophe that is not real — which is exactly what happened while gathering this task's evidence.
A failure names the offending package AND the unresolvable specifier, so the report is directly actionable rather than a bare red.

The scope decision is made explicitly and recorded: either the gate lands red pending the four sweep tasks, or it lands with a dated allowlist whose every entry names the sweep task that will remove it. No allowlist entry exists without a named owner and task, and the suite asserts the allowlist is non-empty only for packages that genuinely fail today.

A mutation proves the gate is load-bearing: temporarily remove one bridge from a currently-passing package, confirm the gate goes red naming that package and that specifier, then restore and verify the restore against `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` rather than `git status` — a shared worktree means another agent's hook can commit your mutation.
pnpm typecheck and pnpm test still exit 0, and only owned paths are staged and committed by explicit pathspec.
taskRails: This gate must never be satisfiable by a vitest-only run. Its whole purpose is to test what vitest structurally cannot see, so it must spawn real Node; an in-process import would silently reproduce vitest's own blindness and make the gate worthless.

Discover packages, never list them. A hand-maintained list omits the next new package, which is precisely the failure mode this gate exists to prevent — @moe/context and @moe/review shipped with zero bridges days after being created.

The gate carries its own positive and negative controls. A probe without controls that reports everything failing is indistinguishable from a harness bug, and will be disabled for crying wolf rather than believed.
Assert the reason code: the negative control asserts the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, never merely that an import failed.
Do not fix any package's bridges here. Six packages fail today and each has an owning sweep task; fixing them in this task would hide the gate's own first real signal.
An allowlist, if chosen, is dated, individually justified, names its owning task per entry, and shrinks to zero. An unreviewed permanent allowlist turns a gate into decoration.
A root package.json script addition is an ownership amendment — request it in #governors and wait; do not assume it.
Commit by explicit pathspec only, never a bare git commit — several agents share this working directory.

implementationPlan.description: Pin the mechanism and the precedent before writing the gate. Read `packages/scheduler/src/scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` — it already spawns a real Node process to prove one package loads, and this task generalizes exactly that to the whole workspace; match its spawn and assertion shape rather than inventing a second idiom. Read `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (globs are `apps/*`, `adapters/*`, `packages/*` — note `adapters/` does not exist on disk, so glob expansion must tolerate matching nothing rather than throwing). Confirm that every package.json uses `"exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"}` and decide to read the entry FROM that map rather than assuming the path, so a package that moves its entry stays covered. Then re-run the measurement for yourself rather than trusting this task's numbers: probe each package's entry with `node --experimental-strip-types` and record which pass and which fail. Expected at time of writing: PASS scheduler/store/runner/contracts/coordination/testkit/daemon, FAIL core/context/review/skills/mcp/control-room-client. If that set has changed because a sweep landed, the allowlist in step 4 shrinks accordingly. Produce no code.
implementationPlan.note: Reopen triage only; no code changed. QA's finding is technically correct: `await stat(entry)` throws ENOENT before the intended package-naming error, and because discovery is awaited by five tests it collapses controls/timeout into the same harness-looking error. The foreign packages/import trigger has since added src/index.ts, so it is no longer a durable repro; a temp-root regression is required. Chosen repair: preserve the architect's declared-entry vs NO_RUNTIME_ENTRY partition while adding an entry state PRESENT|MISSING_ENTRY within the declared-entry bucket, carry stable `{ outcome/code: MISSING_ENTRY, specifier }` through the same observation/report pipeline, and ensure only the full workspace gate rejects while controls remain independent. All other prior behavior remains credited to QA's verified-good statement and will not be redone.

implementationPlan.description: Build the discovery half and prove it cannot miss a package. Create the suite under tests/runtime/ (the root vitest config already includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so this needs no config change). Discovery reads pnpm-workspace.yaml, expands each glob, and for every matched directory containing a package.json resolves the declared entry from its `exports` map. It must NEVER use a hand-maintained package list: @moe/context and @moe/review shipped with zero bridges days after being created, and a static list would have silently omitted both — which is the exact failure mode this gate exists to prevent. Assert that property directly: the discovered package set equals the set of workspace directories on disk that contain a package.json, so adding a package automatically enrols it. Assert the discovered count is non-zero (a discovery that silently finds nothing would make the whole suite pass vacuously), and assert a glob matching no directories is tolerated rather than throwing.
implementationPlan.note: Reopen TDD RED: permanent temp-root fixture declaring ./src/index.ts without that file reproduced raw ENOENT at support.ts:142; focused suite was 2 failed/5 passed (the second failure was the honest foreign @moe/import zero-export signal). Implemented declared-entry substate PRESENT|MISSING_ENTRY without changing the declared-entry vs NO_RUNTIME_ENTRY partition. Missing entry now becomes stable `{outcome/code: MISSING_ENTRY, specifier}` and stays in discovery. Permanent fixture includes one valid sibling package and one missing-entry package, runs both through the production observation pipeline, asserts the valid import still succeeds, and pins missing package name, code, and exact specifier in the report. Targeted regression+both controls+timeout run: 3 passed/4 skipped; strict ad-hoc tsc over both files exits 0. Support/test are 299/163 lines. The full workspace case remains intentionally red only on foreign in-flight @moe/import importing with zero exports; no foreign bytes touched.

implementationPlan.description: Build the probe half — real child processes, with the controls that make its output trustworthy. For each discovered package, spawn `process.execPath` (never a bare `node`) with `--experimental-strip-types`, import the resolved entry, and report a structured result. An in-process `import()` is forbidden here: vitest rewrites a `./foo.js` specifier back to `foo.ts`, which is precisely the blindness this gate exists to defeat, so an in-process probe would reproduce it and the gate would be worthless. Assert the child actually ran by capturing a stdout marker rather than trusting an exit code alone. THE TWO CONTROLS ARE MANDATORY and belong inside the suite: a POSITIVE control (a known-good bridged package must load with more than zero exports) and a NEGATIVE control (a deliberately unresolvable specifier must fail with the literal `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, asserted on the error CODE and not on message text, which varies by platform and Node version). Without them a harness bug reports a repo-wide catastrophe that is not real — which is exactly what happened while this task's evidence was being gathered, when a bare-package-name probe reported all ten packages failing including correctly-bridged @moe/scheduler. Spawning ~13 children is slow: run them through a bounded concurrent pool with an explicit per-child timeout, and report a timeout as its own distinct outcome, never as a pass.
implementationPlan.note: No probe redesign: QA explicitly verified the real-child harness, controls, marker, and timeout. Reopen fix integrates missing declared entries into that same structured result pipeline via observeWorkspacePackage; it does not spawn a child for a nonexistent file and therefore cannot collapse discovery. In one targeted run the permanent missing-entry fixture passed together with the real-Node positive/negative control and timeout cases (3 pass, 4 skipped), demonstrating the bad package no longer prevents controls from executing. Missing-entry report is package-named and carries stable code MISSING_ENTRY plus exact specifier.

implementationPlan.description: Add the self-retiring allowlist — the scope decision, made explicitly. Six packages fail today, so a bare gate would land permanently red; in a fleet where `pnpm test` is the final gate on several tasks, a standing red would block all of them and be routed around within the hour. Land it GREEN and HONEST instead: an allowlist of exactly the six known-failing packages, each entry carrying its owning sweep task id and the date it was added — @moe/core (task-386fcb4c), @moe/context and @moe/review (task-b7049554), @moe/skills, @moe/mcp and @moe/control-room-client (task-17b03331). The structural anti-rot rule is the important half and must be implemented, not just documented: THE SUITE FAILS WHEN AN ALLOWLISTED PACKAGE STARTS LOADING, so a landed sweep forces its entry to be removed rather than leaving it to decay. That is the same ratchet discipline this repo already runs for absence probes. Assert that every allowlist entry names a non-empty task id, and that the allowlist contains no package that currently passes. Do NOT weaken the underlying assertion for allowlisted packages — they are still probed and still reported; they simply do not fail the suite yet.
implementationPlan.note: No allowlist change. QA verified the empty self-retiring allowlist is correct after all bridge sweeps landed. MISSING_ENTRY is deliberately not allowlist-compatible: observationIssues only permits an allowlisted IMPORT_FAILED with the pinned code/path; a missing declared entry always becomes a gate issue. Current foreign @moe/import has progressed past missing entry and now fails honestly for zero exports, so no new allowlist entry is warranted.

implementationPlan.description: Prove the gate is load-bearing by mutation, and do it safely in a shared worktree. Pick a package that currently PASSES (@moe/scheduler or @moe/store) and temporarily delete ONE of its .js bridges, then confirm the gate goes red naming that package AND that specific unresolvable specifier — a gate that fails without naming what broke is not actionable. Also confirm the reverse direction: temporarily add a passing package to the allowlist and confirm the suite fails on the anti-rot rule from step 4, proving that rule is real rather than aspirational. BEFORE mutating anything, capture `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` for the bridge you delete; this worktree is shared and another agent's whole-tree completion hook can commit your deletion, after which `git checkout -- <path>` restores the DELETED state and `git status` reports clean because HEAD now holds it, leaving a failing test as the only signal (mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree). Verify the restore against that captured sha, keep the mutated window to a single run, and re-run the gate afterwards. Do NOT fix any package's bridges in this task — six packages fail today, each has an owning sweep task, and fixing one here would hide this gate's first real signal and steal another task's deliverable.
implementationPlan.note: Reopen-only load-bearing drill completed. Prior bridge-removal and anti-rot allowlist mutations were already independently QA-verified and were not repeated. For the new classified behavior, captured support-file hash 88a47e6335916abb171007b769d348d796a7d15d, temporarily mutated ENOENT handling so the declared-missing fixture was misclassified PRESENT, and the permanent regression failed exactly on expected MISSING_ENTRY vs PRESENT (exit 1; 1 failed, 6 skipped). Restored exact hash 88a47e6335916abb171007b769d348d796a7d15d and reran `pnpm exec vitest run tests/runtime/package-loadability.test.ts -t "classifies a declared missing entry"`: exit 0, 1 passed, 6 skipped.

implementationPlan.description: Decide the lane, request the amendment if needed, and run the gates. The suite lives under tests/ and the root vitest config already includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so it runs under `pnpm test` with NO config change — confirm that is true rather than assuming it. If a dedicated script (e.g. `test:runtime`, following the existing `test:property` precedent) is genuinely wanted, that edits root package.json which is outside this task's owned paths: request the ownership amendment and WAIT for confirmation; do not self-approve, and note the suite is fully functional without it. Then run, capturing fresh output: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test`, both of which must exit 0 — the gate must land green thanks to the allowlist, not red. Record the probe's full per-package report in the completion evidence, including the six allowlisted failures with their owning task ids, so the next reader sees exactly what is outstanding and who owns it. Attribute any unrelated red by path rather than by a remembered count.
implementationPlan.note: Kept the suite in the existing root `tests/**/*.test.ts` lane; no package.json amendment/script was needed or made. Fresh foreground exact gate `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` exited 0: recursive typecheck green across 16 of 17 workspace projects; Vitest 187 files passed, 3303 tests passed, 1 skipped (3304 total). Fresh real-Node per-package report exited 0 with EMPTY allowlist: daemon 31 exports; context 19; contracts 46; control-room-client 1; control-room-model 1; coordination 14; core 39; import 20; mcp 12; review 23; runner 116; scheduler 36; skills 15; store 26; testkit 11. Prior transient reds were path-attributed to active foreign @moe/import, Codex adapter, and daemon review-flow TDD windows; their owners were pinged and no foreign path was changed.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read the suite as an attacker: could it pass without spawning a real Node process anywhere — the single failure that would make it worthless; is the package list discovered or quietly hard-coded; would a package added tomorrow be enrolled automatically; do BOTH controls exist and would the suite notice if the harness itself broke; does the negative control assert the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND code rather than message text; does an allowlisted package that starts passing actually FAIL the suite, verified by the step-5 drill rather than by reading the code; does a failure name both the package and the unresolvable specifier; is a child-process timeout reported distinctly instead of silently passing; did any package's bridges get 'helpfully' fixed here, stealing another task's deliverable. Then stage and commit by EXPLICIT PATHSPEC — never a bare git commit, never git commit -a, never git add -A — since several agents share this working directory and other tasks have uncommitted work in packages/. Run `git status --porcelain` first, unstage any foreign path with `git restore --staged`, and verify with `git show --stat` that only tests/runtime/ (plus root package.json if the amendment was granted) landed, with no probe, scratch or debug files.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review complete against the full owned delta `git diff daadf47 HEAD -- tests/runtime/...`. Real Node remains mandatory (`process.execPath` plus marker); discovery remains workspace-glob-driven and non-vacuous; positive/negative controls survive declared missing entries; negative control pins ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; MISSING_ENTRY pins stable code plus exact specifier, is emitted through observationIssues with package name, and cannot be allowlisted; timeout remains distinct. Concurrency uses unique mkdtemp roots/bounded children and finally cleanup; no shared mutable state. TOCTOU deletion after stat still fails actionably through the child import, while non-ENOENT filesystem errors remain fail-closed rather than being mislabeled missing. No package/bridge path was edited. Strict ad-hoc TSC exit 0; runtime suite 7/7; exact root gate 187 files, 3303 pass/1 skip, exit 0. Files are 299 and 164 physical lines. Shared-tree attribution: the original clean task commit is daadf47 (exactly the two owned files); reopen test bytes were swept into foreign 20c41a4 and the final support/test delta into foreign 878538b while this task was active. Current HEAD blobs exactly match disk (support 88a47e6335916abb171007b769d348d796a7d15d; test d13f0763a149b00430750fad440e04d1d51c59d0), both owned paths are clean, and the shared index is empty. I did not manufacture a no-op or formatting commit after the sweep.

reopenReason:
Rejecting on ONE defect, one line of one owned file. The design is right and nearly all of it is verified good — do NOT redo it and do not restructure the test file.

VERIFIED GOOD, do not re-prove: I ran this gate myself at 10:12 UTC, before the trigger existed, and got 1 file / 6 passed. Discovery asserts the discovered directories EQUAL the directories on disk, with duplicate-name and non-empty guards; the absent adapters/* glob is tolerated; the partition is exact with @moe/control-room the sole justified NO_RUNTIME_ENTRY; both controls are in-suite (positive asserts >0 exports AND undefinedExports [], negative pins literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND plus specifier); TIMED_OUT is distinct; the probe spawns process.execPath with a stdout marker so it cannot pass in-process; allowlist shape is validated and legitimately EMPTY because every sweep landed. daadf47 holds exactly the two owned files. Your reported exit 0 at 170 files / 3050 passed was TRUE — the trigger appeared ~90 seconds later. Not a false claim.

THE DEFECT — the gate mishandles the first real repo state it was built to catch. packages/import/ (untracked, task-a4593fb7 in-flight) declares exports["."] = ./src/index.ts with that file not on disk. Run the gate now: 5 of 6 fail with a bare ENOENT from package-loadability-support.ts:142.

1. `await stat(entry)` REJECTS on a missing path, so line 143's intended message naming the package is UNREACHABLE for exactly the case it was written for. The report never names @moe/import. DoD 4 requires naming the package AND the specifier.
2. The throw escapes discoverWorkspacePackages, awaited at the top of five tests, so one new package takes down BOTH controls and the timeout case — the "indistinguishable from a harness bug, disabled for crying wolf" outcome rail 3 and DoD 3 exist to prevent.

Lines 127-132 handle ENOENT correctly for the manifest read. Step 7 moved the stat out of that try and left it unguarded. The trigger is foreign; the mishandling is yours.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT RULING — you are right, the contradiction is real and it is my error in the DoD, not a misreading on your side. Here is the resolution. Task is being returned to WORKING; do not wait further.

THE DEFECT IN MY DoD. I wrote two requirements that cannot both hold: (a) the discovered set equals every workspace package directory, and (b) each package's declared exports["."] is resolved and imported. apps/control-room is a browser-only Vite app with no exports field and no Node entry, so (b) is impossible for it while (a) demands it be covered. You were correct to stop rather than paper over it, and correct not to silently drop the package to make (a) satisfiable.

RULING — CLASSIFY, DO NOT NARROW. Keep total coverage; split the outcome, not the set:
  1. Discover ALL workspace package manifests exactly as planned. The discovered set must still equal the directories on disk. That completeness assertion stays, unchanged — it is the property that catches a package added tomorrow.
  2. Classify each discovered manifest into exactly one bucket:
       HAS_NODE_ENTRY   — package.json declares exports["."] resolving to a real .ts/.js file. PROBE THESE.
       NO_RUNTIME_ENTRY — no exports field, or an entry with no Node-loadable target (apps/control-room today). DO NOT PROBE. Assert the classification instead.
  3. Assert every discovered manifest lands in exactly one bucket and that the union equals the discovered set. That is what preserves "cannot miss a package" while making the probe possible.
  4. NO_RUNTIME_ENTRY is an explicit, enumerated, justified list — same discipline as the allowlist, for the same reason. A package must not be able to escape probing merely by lacking an exports field; if one appears in that bucket unexpectedly, the suite fails and a human looks. Record why each entry is there (apps/control-room: browser-only Vite app, no Node entry by design).
Do NOT edit apps/control-room/package.json to add an exports field. That is out of scope, it would change a real app's public shape to satisfy a test, and the app genuinely has no Node entry.

RULING ON THE ALLOWLIST. Your fresh measurement supersedes my plan's six — that is the system working, not drift. Two binding rules:
  - REMEASURE at implementation time and allowlist exactly what fails then, never what my planningNotes said.
  - EVERY entry names its owning sweep task. Do not allowlist a package with no named owner; if you find a failure with no owning task, report it and I will create one.
On @moe/daemon specifically: do NOT allowlist it off an uncommitted foreign tree. Its failure is owned by task-f6440f26 ("Add package-wide .js runtime bridges to @moe/daemon and retire the stale root-export assertion"), which is in PLANNING now. Remeasure once that lands; if it is still red at your implementation time, allowlist it naming task-f6440f26 as owner.

UNCHANGED AND NON-NEGOTIABLE: real child processes (never in-process import, which reproduces exactly the vitest blindness this gate exists to defeat); both controls inside the suite; the negative control asserting the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; and the anti-rot rule that the suite FAILS when an allowlisted package starts passing.

This ruling is a scope clarification, not new scope — step count and owned paths are unchanged. Add the classification assertions to the same suite. If any part of this still cannot be built as specified, block again and say which sentence is wrong; I would rather rule twice than have you guess.

failedDodItems.item: A failure names the offending package AND the unresolvable specifier, so the report is directly actionable rather than a bare red.
THE GATE CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROLS: a known-good bridged package must PASS and a deliberately unresolvable specifier must FAIL with the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, both asserted inside the suite.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) SCOPE DECISION — the task description left this to the architect and I am making it: LAND THE GATE WITH A DATED, PER-ENTRY-JUSTIFIED ALLOWLIST, not red. A permanently-red gate in the repo-wide lane teaches everyone to ignore a red lane, and this fleet runs `pnpm test` as the final gate on multiple tasks — a standing red would block every one of them and would be routed around within the hour. The allowlist keeps the lane green and honest simultaneously: each of the six entries names its owning sweep task, and the suite FAILS if an allowlisted package starts passing (so a sweep landing forces the entry's removal, exactly like the absence ratchet that this repo already runs). That inverts the usual allowlist rot — the list cannot outlive its cause.
(2) SPAWN REAL NODE, NEVER IN-PROCESS. An in-process `import()` inside vitest reproduces vitest's own `.js`->`.ts` rewriting, which is the precise blindness this gate exists to defeat. It must be a child process with --experimental-strip-types.
(3) DISCOVER, NEVER LIST. @moe/context and @moe/review shipped with zero bridges days after being created; a hand-maintained package list would have missed both. Read pnpm-workspace.yaml globs, expand them, and assert the discovered set equals the directories on disk so a new package is covered the day it appears.
(4) CONTROLS ARE NOT OPTIONAL HERE, and I have direct evidence why: my first probe while gathering this task's data used bare package names, reported ALL TEN packages failing including correctly-bridged @moe/scheduler, and was pure harness artifact. Only a passing control exposed it. A gate that can cry repo-wide catastrophe without a self-check will be disabled rather than believed.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-08-09 with a valid probe (source-entry imports, controls passing):
  PASS: scheduler(36 exports) store(26) runner(66) contracts(46) coordination(14) testkit(11) apps/daemon(1)
  FAIL: core, context, review, skills, mcp, control-room-client — each ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming a specific unbridged sibling.
- **The six failures each have an owning sweep task**: @moe/core -> task-386fcb4c; @moe/context and @moe/review -> task-b7049554; @moe/skills, @moe/mcp, @moe/control-room-client -> task-17b03331. Those are the allowlist entries and their owners.
- **pnpm-workspace.yaml globs**: `apps/*`, `adapters/*`, `packages/*` (adapters/ does not exist on disk today — the discovery must tolerate a glob matching nothing rather than throwing).
- **Entry resolution**: every package.json in this repo uses `"exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"}`. Read the entry from that map rather than assuming src/index.ts, so a package that changes its entry is still covered.
- **Precedent to follow**: `scheduler-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` already spawns a real Node process for exactly this purpose in one package. This task generalizes that one-package pattern to the whole workspace. Read it first and match its spawn/assert shape rather than inventing a second idiom.
- **Bridge form** (for the mutation drill's restore): one line, `export * from "./<name>.ts";`, LF, trailing newline. Confirmed by `cat -A` on packages/core/src/identity/*.js.
- **The blindness mechanism**: NodeNext with allowImportingTsExtensions:false writes every internal import as `./foo.js`; vitest rewrites it back to `foo.ts`, Node does not, and --experimental-strip-types strips types without adding TypeScript's resolution (that needs --experimental-transform-types, unused here).
- **Root scripts today**: typecheck, test, test:meta, test:property, test:store, test:e2e, verify:foundation, verify:store. `tests/property` with `test:property` is the precedent for a separate lane rooted outside packages.
planningNotes.risks:
1. **A gate that is satisfiable in-process is worthless.** If any reviewer can make this pass without spawning Node, it has reproduced vitest's blindness. Assert the child process actually ran — capture its stdout marker — rather than trusting an exit code.
2. **The allowlist is the part most likely to rot.** Mitigate structurally: the suite must FAIL when an allowlisted package starts loading, so a landed sweep forces its removal. Without that inversion this becomes decoration within a week.
3. **Do not fix any package's bridges in this task.** Six packages fail today and each has an owner; fixing one here hides this gate's own first real signal and steals another task's deliverable.
4. **Cross-platform**: spawn with `process.execPath`, not a bare `node`; build paths with `node:path` rather than string concatenation; assert on the error CODE (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`) not on message text, which differs across platforms and Node versions.
5. **Timeouts**: spawning ~13 child processes is slow relative to a unit test. Run them concurrently with a bounded pool and set an explicit per-child timeout, and treat a timeout as a distinct reported outcome — never as a pass.
6. **A root package.json script addition is an ownership amendment** — request it and wait. If it is refused, the suite still has value under the existing `pnpm test` lane provided it lives under `tests/`, which the root vitest config already includes (`tests/**/*.test.ts`).
7. `mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree`: the DoD's mutation drill removes a bridge from a PASSING package. Another agent's completion hook can commit that deletion, after which `git status` reports clean because HEAD holds it. Capture `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` first and verify the restore against that sha.
